chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the vineyard (or fruit-bearing land), when is its sale permissible? He said: 'When it sets (the fruit) and becomes 'Uqud'. And 'Uqud' is the name of Al-Hisrm in the Nabataean (Syriac) language.

key_terms.الْحِصْرِمُ: The stage of fruit maturity where it is firm and distinct from the blossom
key_terms.عَقَدَ: It set (referring to fruit setting on the tree)
key_terms.عُقُوداً: A state of firmness/maturity in fruit

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to sell fruit before it is fully ripe according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of selling fruit crops once they reach the stage of 'Uqud', a term derived from Syriac/Nabataean denoting firm, distinct fruit. This ruling clarifies the transition from uncertainty (gharar) to tangible ownership, a key principle in Shia commercial jurisprudence regarding agricultural produce.
